claims.subject: Escape crystal
claims.value: 1 free at start; 10,000 coins each from Death, Rick (Wizards' Tower) or the Mysterious Stranger
claims.statement: Every Hardcore Worlds character starts with one escape crystal. More cost 10,000 coins from Death, Rick or the Mysterious Stranger.

sources.title: Hardcore Worlds
sources.quote: All players begin with a free [[escape crystal]]. More may be purchased from Death himself, [[Rick (Wizards' Tower)|Rick]] at the [[Wizards' Tower]], or the [[Mysterious Stranger]] in [[Ver Sinhaza]] for {{coins|10000}} each.

sources.title: Update:Hardcore Worlds - OUT TODAY
sources.quote: First is that you can buy [https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Escape_crystal Escape Crystals] from him for 10,000 coins.

claims.subject: Escape crystal

value.auto_activation: on taking damage (including 0s) after a configured inactivity of 2-300 seconds

claims.statement: An escape crystal can be set to auto-teleport the player when they take damage (including 0s) after 2-300 seconds of inactivity. It also fires at once if the player takes damage just after logging in or hopping worlds.

sources.title: Escape crystal
sources.quote: Additionally, the crystal can be configured to auto-activate upon taking damage (including zeros) after a specified time of inactivity (ranging from 2 to 300 seconds) via the "Configure" option

sources.title: Update:Hardcore Worlds Are Coming On November 4th
sources.quote: which can activate automatically when there's been no input for a while, essentially helping you out of situations where you might have disconnected or your device crashes!

claims.subject: Escape crystal
claims.value: does not activate while the player is moving
claims.statement: The escape crystal does NOT activate while the player is moving. If the inactivity time is reached mid-movement, it activates only when the player stops. Agility obstacles and run paths are movement.

sources.title: Escape crystal
sources.quote: The crystal will '''NOT''' activate while the player is moving. If the inactive time is reached at any point during movement, the crystal will activate when the player stops moving.

claims.notes: Whether forced movement during an obstacle animation (e.g. a deathslide) counts as 'moving' was not found; treat the crystal as no protection against single-hit obstacle damage.

claims.subject: Escape crystal
claims.value: works up to level 30 Wilderness only
claims.statement: Escape crystal teleports work up to level 30 Wilderness. The Wilderness Agility Course (levels 50-56) is above that, so the crystal cannot get the player out there.

sources.title: Escape crystal
sources.quote: It is one of the [[Wilderness#Member_teleportation_up_to_level_30_Wilderness|few items]] whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of [[teleport]]ation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

claims.subject: Escape crystal
claims.value: clears poison, burn and other status effects when activated (announced)
claims.statement: Jagex announced that escape crystals would clear poison, burn and other status effects when activated.

sources.title: Update:Hardcore Worlds Are Coming On November 4th
sources.quote: Finally, we'd let the Crystals clear poison, burn or any other status effects if activated

claims.notes: Worded as an intention ('we'd let') in the pre-launch post. The escape crystal wiki page (rev 15409296) does not list this change, so it is unconfirmed in game.

claims.subject: Disconnect during combat
claims.statement: If a player disconnects unexpectedly while in combat, the character stays in the game for up to 60 seconds and can keep taking hits before it is logged out.

sources.title: Logout button
sources.quote: This works because of a 60 second timer before the game forcibly logs you out after an unexpected disconnection during combat.

claims.subject: Logout in combat
claims.statement: A player cannot log out until 16 ticks (9.6 seconds) after they last received a hit.

sources.title: Logout button
sources.quote: Players may click the logout button at any time, although players in [[combat]] cannot log out until 16 game [[Game tick|ticks]], or 9.6 seconds, after they have last received a hit.

claims.subject: Wilderness Agility Course
claims.value: x-logging does not work in singles-plus combat
claims.statement: X-logging (closing the client to escape a PKer) does not work in singles-plus combat areas, which include the Wilderness Agility Course.

sources.title: Logout button
sources.quote: this will not work in [[Singles-plus combat]]

sources.title: Singles-plus combat
sources.quote: * the [[Wilderness Agility Course]]

claims.subject: Owner's character (brief stats)
claims.statement: From the brief's verified stats (Def 1, HP 48, Prayer 44, Ranged 56, Atk 44, Str 32, Mag 44), the character is combat level 45 (Ranged-based), not ~60.

sources.title: Combat level
sources.quote: \text{Final} &= \lfloor \text{Base} + \textrm{max}(\text{Melee}, \text{Range}, \text{Mage}) \rfloor

claims.notes: Computed: base=17.75, range=27.300, melee=24.700, mage=21.450, so floor(45.050) = 45. The dispatch's '~60' is wrong for these stats.

claims.subject: Level-based monster aggression
claims.value: aggressive if player combat level <= 2 x monster level; vs combat 45 every level-based aggressive monster of level 23+ attacks
claims.statement: Level-based aggressive monsters attack players whose combat level is at most twice their own. At combat 45, any such monster of level 23 or higher attacks (2 x 23 = 46).

sources.title: Aggressiveness
sources.quote: When aggressiveness is based on combat level, an aggressive monster will attack a player whose combat level is less than or equal to twice the monster's level.

claims.subject: Monster aggression tolerance
claims.value: aggressive monsters become tolerant after 10 minutes in the area; leaving and returning resets it
claims.statement: After 10 minutes near aggressive monsters they become tolerant, but leaving and returning resets this. Most Wilderness monsters are aggressive regardless of level.

sources.title: Aggressiveness
sources.quote: After a player spends 10 minutes in the vicinity of aggressive monsters, the monsters will become [[tolerant]] of the player and become passive.

sources.title: Aggressiveness
sources.quote: *Most monsters in the [[Wilderness]] are aggressive regardless of level.

claims.subject: Wilderness Agility Course
claims.statement: The Wilderness Agility Course lies in level 50-56 Wilderness.

sources.title: Wilderness Agility Course
sources.quote: |wilderness = 50-56

claims.subject: Wilderness Agility Course
claims.value: singles-plus; players can attack even while you are fighting a monster
claims.statement: The whole course is dangerous: it is a singles-plus area where player killers can attack at any time, even while you are already in combat with a monster.

sources.title: Wilderness Agility Course
sources.quote: '''{{Colour|Red|The entire course is dangerous}}''', taking place in a [[singles-plus combat]] area that allows [[player killers]] to attack at any time, '''even if you are already in combat with a monster'''.

claims.subject: Wilderness Agility Course
claims.statement: Players within combat level +/- the Wilderness level can attack. A combat-45 player at the course (level 50-56) can be attacked by any player from combat 3 up to 95-101.

sources.title: Wilderness
sources.quote: This range is calculated by taking the [[combat]] level and adding or subtracting the current Wilderness level.

claims.notes: Range computed: 45-50 < 3 (the minimum), 45+50 = 95, 45+56 = 101.

claims.subject: Wilderness Agility Course: Ropeswing
claims.statement: Failing the WAC ropeswing deals floor(current_hp*0.15)+1 damage (8 at 48 HP). It scales with current HP, so it cannot kill on its own.

sources.title: Wilderness Agility Course
sources.quote: Can be failed, which will send the player down to the [[Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon|dungeon]] below and deal <math>\left\lfloor\text{Current hitpoints}\times0.15\right\rfloor+1</math> damage.

claims.subject: Wilderness Agility Course: Stepping stone
claims.statement: Failing the WAC stepping stone deals floor(current_hp*0.2)+1 damage (10 at 48 HP). It scales with current HP, so it cannot kill on its own.

sources.title: Wilderness Agility Course
sources.quote: You can only fail on the third stone, which deals <math>\left\lfloor\text{Current hitpoints}\times0.2\right\rfloor+1</math> damage.

claims.subject: Wilderness Agility Course: Log balance
claims.statement: Failing the WAC log balance deals floor(current_hp*0.15)+1 damage (8 at 48 HP). It scales with current HP, so it cannot kill on its own.

sources.title: Wilderness Agility Course
sources.quote: Can be failed, which will send the player down to the dungeon below and deal <math>\left\lfloor\text{Current hitpoints}\times0.15\right\rfloor+1</math> damage.

claims.subject: Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon
claims.statement: A failed ropeswing or log balance drops the player into the dungeon below (level 53-56 Wilderness), which holds eight level 25 skeletons (max hit 4, aggressive).

sources.title: Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon
sources.quote: It covers level 53 to 56 Wilderness. The dungeon entrance is a ladder in the north-east corner of the Agility course, which is past the rope swing and before the stepping stones. The dungeon contains eight [[skeleton]]s and four [[bones|bone]] [[item spawn|spawns]].

However, the [[Teleport Block]] spell will prevent using nearly any means of teleportation for five minutes, or two and a half minutes if it is successfully cast on a player with [[Protect from Magic]] active.

gaps: Hallowed Sepulchre trap damage per floor (wizard fire, knight swords, crossbow bolts) is not on the wiki. Only 'a small amount of damage' and 'recommended 70+ HP'.
Failure damage on the Seers' Village (gap 1, tightrope), Ardougne (gaps 1-2) and Canifis (gap 3) rooftops is not documented on the pinned pages.

Disconnect behaviour for the Hallowed Sepulchre, the rooftop courses, the Agility Pyramid and the Colossal Wyrm course is not documented beyond the general 60-second in-combat rule.
How close the Avium Savannah jaguars are to the Colossal Wyrm course and its teleport landing is not established.
Creature of Fenkenstrain fight NPCs (level 51 and 72) were not identified by name or max hit.
The upcoming Graveyard Agility course (65/80) has no hazard data; it is unreleased.

Hazards of high-requirement Agility-XP quests (Dragon Slayer II, Song of the Elves, Mourning's End II, Monkey Madness II, Secrets of the North, Beneath Cursed Sands, Curse of Arrav, Making Friends with My Arm, Icthlarin's Little Helper, Underground Pass, Land of the Goblins, Heart of Darkness, RFD Awowogei) were not researched. No second independent (T3) source was gathered for any max hit or damage formula.

decisions.decision: Classify every Agility activity (rooftops, Werewolf, Ape Atoll, Pyramid, Brimhaven Arena, Hallowed Sepulchre, WAC, Colossal Wyrm, Dorgesh-Kaan) as UNSAFE_DEATH.
decisions.reason: The T1 Jagex posts give an exhaustive safe list (Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, FT 4th phase, Fight Caves and Zulrah diary resurrections, Fight Pit) plus the '99% of deaths' framing; no Agility activity is on it, and the charter makes UNSAFE the default without a T1 safe source.
alternatives_considered: Use the HCIM safe-death list (rejected: HW uses the stricter HGIM ruleset)
Leave unclassified (rejected: dispatch asks for a class per activity)

decisions.decision: Use combat level 45 (computed) rather than the dispatch's '~60' for aggression checks.
decisions.reason: The brief's verified stats give combat 45 by the wiki formula, and aggression thresholds depend on it (e.g. Pollnivneach jackals, level 23+ monsters).
alternatives_considered: Use ~60 as dispatched (rejected: contradicts sealed brief stats)

decisions.decision: Record 'not documented' instead of numbers for Seers/Ardougne/Canifis rooftop, Ape Atoll and Sepulchre per-floor damage.
decisions.reason: The pinned wiki pages give no figures; the constitution forbids guessing.
alternatives_considered: Use community figures from memory (rejected: memory is not a source)

decisions.decision: Include quest fights only for quests that award Agility XP or unlock candidate courses, as listed by 'Quest experience rewards' rev 15408569.
decisions.reason: Coverage of what a planner could plausibly use, without trivia; quests already in the owner's list are excluded.
alternatives_considered: Cover every Agility-XP quest including Dragon Slayer II, Song of the Elves, MEP2 and Secrets of the North (rejected: requirements far out of reach; noted in gaps)

decisions.decision: Mark the escape crystal's 'clears poison/status effects' change as medium confidence.
decisions.reason: It appears only as a stated intention in the 22 Oct T1 post; the item page's change log does not record it.
